To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the numbers to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2} & \ge -4x \\ -{x}^{2}+4x & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y=-{x}^{2}+4x$ lies above the $x$-axis or touches this axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+4x & =0 \\ -x(x-4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=0$ and $x=4,$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004892/assets/d234c29de2a39c664d6a03acf1d8cc43782914a3c82045cc103353ebaf67b897.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
-{x}^{2}+4x\ge 0,
$$

we look for the part of the parabola that is above the $x$-axis or touches this axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $0\le x\le 4.$ 

Using interval notation, we write $x\in [0,4].$
